newsitem.title: USA: First of America to sell 20 branches.
newsitem.headline: First of America to sell 20 branches.

text.p: First of America Bank Corp. said Friday it will sell 15 branches in Michigan and five branches in Illinois as part of the Midwest banking company's strategy to streamline operations.
The Michigan branches includes eight that the Kalamazoo, Mich.-based company had announced it would sell in August.

First of America said gains from the sales should add about $20 million to $25 million to its non-interest income in the fourth quarter and raise earnings per share by about 20 cents to 25 cents, it said.

"We continue to analyse our branch network and retail delivery systems in order to bring products and services directly and profitably to our customers the way they want them delivered," said Richard Chormann, chairman, president and chief executive officer.

"These steps provide us with the opportunity to increase the efficiency of our product distribution system going forward, and with the opening of 25 supermarket branches during the first six months of 1996, reinvest in new delivery channels," he said.

During the first quarter of 1996, First of America sold three branches in Illinois and one in Michigan, resulting in $4.4 million in gains. The additional branch sales will reduce total deposits by about $375 million, or 2 percent.
First of America has $15 billion in loans and $18 billion in deposits and serves over 3.2 million households in Michigan, Indiana, Illinois and Florida.
Its stock rose 87.5 cents to $51.375 on the New York Stock Exchange in late morning trading.
